name: classic french lentils
instructions:
The classic french le puy lentil side — no gravy core, no cream: aromatics, whole lentils cooked firm-tender in stock, and a dijon-vinegar finish. INSTAPOT recipe, starting from DRIED LE PUY LENTILS. Cooked once — the dijon + red wine vinegar finish is the VARIANT A BASELINE (see notes for first-cook results).

SERVES 4 as a side.

=== INGREDIENTS (DRAFT) ===

- 1 cup dried LE PUY LENTILS, rinsed (the small dark-green french lentils — they hold their shape; don't sub red or brown here)
- 1 small yellow onion (or 2 shallots), fine dice
- 1 carrot, fine dice
- 1 celery stalk, fine dice
- 2-3 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 bay leaf
- thyme (a few fresh sprigs or ~1/2 tsp dried)
- olive oil or butter for the sauté
- 1 3/4 cups chicken stock (water works; stock is better)
- salt (go light if the stock is salted) and black pepper

FINISH:
- 1-2 tsp dijon mustard
- splash of red wine vinegar
- chopped fresh parsley

=== PROCEDURE (DRAFT) ===

1. SAUTÉ MODE: soften the onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil/butter (~5 min). Add the garlic for the last minute.
2. LENTILS IN: add the rinsed le puy lentils, stock, bay leaf, and thyme. Stir once.
3. PRESSURE COOK: HIGH pressure, 12-14 MINUTES TOTAL (tested: 8 min wasn't enough, +3 more was sort of enough). Target: firm-tender lentils that hold their shape — le puy's whole point.
4. FINISH: fish out the bay leaf and thyme stems. Whisk the dijon with the red wine vinegar, fold through the hot lentils. Salt and black pepper to taste; parsley over the top.
5. Serve warm as a side.
notes:
=== FIRST COOK — RESULTS ===

Made for real: chicken stock, lentils, onion/celery/garlic/carrot + bay leaf, sautéed in the pot with olive oil (UNCLEAR IF BUTTER WOULD HAVE BEEN BETTER — open question).

- PRESSURE TIME: 8 minutes on high WASN'T ENOUGH; another 3 was sort of enough. Future: 12-14 MINUTES TOTAL.
- LIQUID IS HARD TO GET RIGHT IN THE INSTAPOT — too easy for it to turn into a soup. Calibration ongoing.
- FLAT WITHOUT TOMATO: tasted a little flat without tomato — RESISTED adding it (this dish's identity is the no-tomato spare french side).
- RESCUE EXPERIMENT: cheese + dried thyme + tarragon helped a lot but didn't taste very unique. (ROSEMARY WOULD BE AWFUL HERE — clashing.)
- THE WINNER: took a fresh spoonful of the flat stuff and tried RED WINE VINEGAR + DIJON MUSTARD — GREAT COMBO. That's the VARIANT A BASELINE.

=== VARIANT A BASELINE ===

The spare build + the dijon + red wine vinegar finish is variant A. Future variants build from here. Overall: not fully satisfied with it yet — has potential, not more.

=== WHERE THE EXPERIMENT SITS — MAY NEED AN IDEOLOGICAL REWORK ===

- OLIVE OIL + SOFFRITO + CHICKEN BROTH: a bit boring.
- CREAM/MUSTARD/VINEGAR: seems to be too much.
- THE FORMAT MIGHT BE THE PROBLEM: I'm making it SUBMERGED IN LIQUID because that's instapot-convenient — but THIS DOESN'T WANT TO BE A STEW. The rework, if it comes, starts there.

=== WHAT THIS RECIPE IS (AND ISN'T) ===

This is the classic preparation the mushroomed-lentils family explicitly ISN'T — no gravy core, no pureed mushrooms, no cream. Whole firm lentils + soffrito + a sharp dijon-vinegar finish. The french-kit logic still shows up (dijon in the finish), but as a bright accent on a spare dish rather than a silent balancer in a rich one.

=== LE PUY SPECIFICALLY ===

Le puy lentils hold their shape through cooking — that's the identity of the dish. Standard brown lentils go soft and muddy the texture; red lentils dissolve entirely (wrong dish).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[french-lentil-salad]]: the cold expression of french lentils (cream vinaigrette + endives). This recipe is the warm classical side.
- [[mushroomed-lentils-french]]: the rich gravy-core cousin — reach for that when you want a stew, this when you want a side.
- [[jaffrey-lentils]]: the indian whole-lentil counterpart.
